transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I came in because... well, I'm having a lot of trouble at work lately. I'm a physical scientist, and I just can't seem to keep my mind on the actual experiments anymore. It's like, if I'm on a grant call or in a safety meeting, I'll suddenly notice a pump vibrating, or hear a student make a side comment, or even just remember some odd peak in an old spectrum. And then I'm just... off. I'll spend hours chasing that completely unrelated thing, while the actual work everyone needs from me just falls apart. It's getting really bad.
Do you feel like you have no control over these distracting thoughts that come into your mind?

I'm not really sure. I haven't really thought about it in terms of having zero control. It's just... they pop into my head, and I follow them. I don't know if I could stop them if I tried, I just haven't really noticed.
Do you feel anxious when these distracting thoughts occur?

No, not really. I wouldn't call it anxiety. I don't feel nervous or panicked when it happens. It's more just... I get completely absorbed in whatever that new thing is. I don't feel anxious about it at the time, I just sort of... go wherever my brain takes me.
Do you ever have thoughts that repeat over and over in your mind, even when you try to think about something else?

No, I don't think so. It's not really a loop, or... or the same thought repeating over and over. I don't get stuck on one specific thing like that. It's really just a constant stream of new things catching my attention, rather than one thought playing on repeat.
Do you often act on impulse, doing things without much consideration for the consequences?

No, I don't really think so. I wouldn't say I'm an impulsive person. I mean... I generally know what the consequences of things are, and I don't just jump into doing something reckless. Even with my mind jumping around to different things, I'm not really acting out on them in a way that ignores the outcome. So, no, I haven't really noticed myself doing that.
Do you have thoughts that you feel compelled to think about, even if you don't want to?

No, I don't think I have anything like that. I don't feel forced to think about certain things against my will. Like I said, it's more that my attention just shifts to whatever new idea pops up, not that I'm trapped thinking about something I'm trying to avoid. So, no, I wouldn't say I feel compelled to think about things.
Do you ever become so focused on a task or activity that you lose track of time and forget about everything else around you?

No, I don't really get hyper-focused like that. I don't get so absorbed in one thing that I lose track of time or my surroundings. Honestly, it's usually the opposite. I have a hard time staying on one task long enough to get that deep into it because my mind is already moving on to the next thing. So, no, I don't really lose myself in activities like that.
Do you feel like your inability to focus on your work is causing you significant stress or problems in your daily life?

Yes, it really is. It's causing a lot of problems, especially at work. My department has actually had to step in on decisions that I used to handle myself. Because my focus has been so off, I've been missing priorities and just... getting all the scheduling confused. 

It's strained my supervision of the lab, to the point where it started putting the project and even our lab safety expectations at risk. So, yes, it's extremely stressful and it's definitely having a major impact right now.
Are your difficulties with focus and staying on task causing problems in your personal relationships?

No, not really. The problems are really just isolated to my work. I haven't noticed my lack of focus causing any issues with my friends or family, or anything like that. It's mostly just the lab where things are falling apart.
Have you been having any trouble sleeping lately?

Well, I wouldn't really call it trouble, because I don't feel tired. But I am sleeping a lot less. Most nights I'm only getting maybe two or three hours of sleep. A lot of times I just end up dozing off on the couch with my laptop still open. 

The thing is, when I wake up, I don't feel groggy at all. I wake up feeling completely sharp and ready to get right back to work. Honestly, lately it just feels like sleep is an inefficient interruption to everything I need to get done.
Are you having difficulty completing everyday tasks or chores outside of work due to your mind wandering?

No, not really. Outside of work, I haven't noticed any issues like that. I can still handle my normal chores and errands just fine. My mind doesn't really wander when I'm doing things around the house or running to the store. It's just at the lab where I'm having all the trouble keeping things straight.
Are you feeling overwhelmed or distressed by your inability to focus at work?

Not really. I wouldn't say I'm distressed or overwhelmed by it at all. I mean, it's more just... inconvenient, I guess? 

I have all these ideas and projects I'm working on in the lab right now, so it's a bit annoying that I can't keep my focus on just one thing to finish it. But I don't feel upset or overwhelmed. I actually feel really good, it's just a matter of getting my notes and experiments organized.
Are you having any difficulty maintaining your current relationships or responsibilities outside of work due to your mind wandering or lack of focus?

No, like I said, outside of the lab, things are fine. My relationships are normal, and I'm keeping up with everything I need to do at home. I'm not having any trouble with my focus when I'm dealing with my personal life or my regular responsibilities. It's really just at work where I'm jumping from one thing to the next.
Do you feel like your difficulties at work are affecting how you feel about yourself?

No, not at all. I don't feel bad about myself. Like I said, I actually feel really good right now. I know I'm smart, and I know my ideas are good. It's just a matter of getting them all down and executed. I don't think less of myself just because I'm having a little trouble keeping my focus on one experiment at a time.
Have you recently taken on more projects or tasks than you usually handle at work?

Yes, I have. I'm actually at the lab before anyone else even arrives right now. I've been... well, I'm rewriting our protocols, rearranging the instrument schedules, emailing collaborators in three different countries, and starting several new analyses all at the same time. 

It just feels like sitting still right now would be wasting the one chance I have to fix everything and get it all moving. So, yes, I'm definitely doing a lot more than usual.
Are you in danger of losing your job due to your inability to focus and stay on task at work?

Well, it's getting to that point, I think. My department has actually had to step in on decisions I used to handle on my own. Because I've been missing priorities and the scheduling has gotten so confused, they felt like I was putting the project at risk. And with the way I've been managing things, they said I was straining the supervision and putting lab safety expectations at risk, too. So, yes, my job is definitely on the line right now.
Are you feeling like your overall well-being or daily life is being negatively impacted by your symptoms?

Well, yes. I mean, like I was just saying about my job... that's a huge part of my daily life. Having my department step in to take over decisions I always used to handle myself is a pretty big deal. They had to intervene because my missed priorities and all the confused scheduling started putting the actual project at risk. And when they tell you that you're straining supervision and compromising lab safety expectations... yeah, I'd definitely say that's a negative impact on my life right now, even if my energy levels feel great.
Do you feel like your lack of focus and constant shifting of attention is causing you significant emotional distress?

Well, to be honest, I'm not really feeling distressed by it emotionally. I actually feel like my mind is working faster and I have all this energy. But... I guess the distress comes more from the consequences of it. Like I mentioned, my department had to step in and take over decisions I normally make. The missed priorities and all the mixed-up scheduling... it got to the point where they said I was putting the project at risk. They even told me I was straining the supervision and that my actions were risking lab safety expectations. So, the situation at work is definitely causing problems, even if I don't feel emotionally upset by the lack of focus itself.
Have you experienced difficulties with focus or restlessness in multiple settings, not just at work?

I'm not really sure. I haven't really noticed it outside of the lab, to be honest. I mean, work is where everything kind of came to a head with the project and the safety expectations. 

If I'm restless or losing focus at home... well, no one's really pointed it out, and I haven't felt like it's a problem there. So, I don't really have a good answer for you on that, other than what's been happening at work.
Have you experienced similar difficulties with focus and distraction throughout your life?

No, not really throughout my whole life. It's just... this has been going on for about seven months. It started right around the time I took over the multi-site spectroscopy project. Before that, I didn't really have these kinds of issues.
